Alice Marble (1913 – 1990) was a world No. 1 American tennis player who won 18 Grand Slam championships (1936–40): 5 in Singles (1 at Wimbledon; 4 at the US Open), 6 in Women's Doubles, and 7 in Mixed Doubles. Near the beginning of her career, Marble contracted a serious case of tuberculosis and considered quitting tennis, but her friends Lombard and Clark spurred her into making, and financed, a come back.

After retirement, she worked on the Editorial Advisory Board of DC Comics and then was recruited as an American spy by the OSS. Her mission involved renewing contact with a former lover, a Swiss banker, and obtaining Nazi financial data. The operation ended when her contact, a Nazi double agent shot her in the back, but she was extracted and recovered.
